answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond, then release it only after the agent completes independently verifiable tasks without triggering disputes. This makes a sybil attack costly: the attacker must fund every identity and keep its bond tied up, while coordinated fake agents risk forfeiture when their claims fail cross-checks. A spiral of identities cannot cheaply mirror a trusted agent’s history, and a mesa of dormant accounts still consumes capital before it can influence votes or markets.
